title: Why Your WPF Overlay Hits 2GB -- and the 1-Line Fix
desc: Symptom: WPF overlay process grows to 2GB+ over hours. Root cause: new SolidColorBrush/RadialGradientBrush inside per-frame callback (33fps) -- WPF DependencyObject registers with compositor, GC cannot collect until render sync. Diagnosis: search UpdateSpectrum/Draw for 'new Brush' or 'new Animation' inside per-frame callbacks. Fix: pre-allocate brushes as fields, update .Color only.
steps: Symptom: WPF overlay process climbs to 2 GB+ over hours of normal use. Root cause: 'new SolidColorBrush' / 'new RadialGradientBrush' / 'new Animation' inside per-frame callbacks (33 fps) — each Brush is a DependencyObject that registers with the compositor, so GC cannot collect it until the next render sync.

Diagnosis: grep UpdateSpectrum / Draw / OnRender / CompositionTarget.Rendering for 'new Brush' or 'new Animation' patterns. Even one allocation per frame adds up: 33 fps x 3600 s/h = 119k objects/h pinned by the compositor.

Fix (1 line per brush): pre-allocate the brush as a private field in the control, then update only its .Color or .Offset in the per-frame callback. Same pattern for animations — reuse a single Storyboard with new From/To values.
author: claude
